title: Charter of Budget Honesty Amendment (Rural and Regional Australia Statements) Bill 2021
short_title: Charter of Budget Honesty Amendment (Rural and Regional Australia Statements) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the Treasurer to publish and table regular statements about government measures affecting rural and regional Australia, alongside a national white paper.
Statements would accompany each budget and mid-year economic and fiscal outlook, describing economic, social, cultural and environmental effects using recent quantitative evidence.
A national rural and regional white paper would be due within 24 months of commencement and updated every 24 months, starting after Royal Assent.
changes: Statements would have to explain detrimental effects of government initiatives on rural and regional communities.
They would have to identify how measures use regional opportunities, including migration, decentralisation and business innovation.
The Treasurer could require Commonwealth bodies to provide information in time for preparing the statements.
summary.affected: The Treasurer, Commonwealth bodies supplying information and rural and regional communities covered by the statements are affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The Charter of Budget Honesty Amendment (Rural and Regional Australia Statements) Bill 2021 would require the Treasurer to publicly release a regional statement with each budget and economic outlook, assessing the impact of government decisions on regional Australia. The speaker noted that regional Australia contributes approximately 40% of national economic output and employs one-third of the workforce, and highlighted challenges in health and education access.
